misconceptions.description: Assignment always makes an independent copy, even for mutable objects.
misconceptions.title: Assignment always copies the value

misconceptions.description: Assignment establishes a persistent algebraic relationship between names.
misconceptions.title: Assignment is an algebraic equation

misconceptions.description: Integer floor division truncates toward zero for negative operands.
misconceptions.title: Floor division truncates toward zero

misconceptions.description: All arithmetic operators are evaluated strictly left to right.
misconceptions.title: Arithmetic is strictly left to right

misconceptions.description: Only literal True/False can control a conditional.
misconceptions.title: Only literal booleans control conditionals

misconceptions.description: Separate if statements act like mutually exclusive elif branches.
misconceptions.title: Separate if statements are mutually exclusive

misconceptions.description: The stop index is included in a slice.
misconceptions.title: Slice stop index is inclusive

misconceptions.description: The first item has index one.
misconceptions.title: Indexing starts at one

misconceptions.description: range includes its stop bound.
misconceptions.title: range includes its stop bound

misconceptions.description: Printing a result makes it the function return value.
misconceptions.title: Returning and printing are the same

misconceptions.description: Assignment inside a function automatically rebinds a same-named global.
misconceptions.title: Local assignment rebinds the global

misconceptions.description: Copying the outer container also copies all nested mutable objects.
misconceptions.title: A shallow copy is a deep copy

misconceptions.description: Iterating a dictionary yields values rather than keys.
misconceptions.title: Dictionary iteration yields values

misconceptions.description: A typed except clause catches every exception.
misconceptions.title: A typed except catches everything

misconceptions.description: Python 3 list-comprehension loop variables overwrite the enclosing variable.
misconceptions.title: Comprehension loop variable leaks

misconceptions.description: A mutable default is created anew for each function call.
misconceptions.title: Mutable defaults are recreated per call

misconceptions.description: Reusing an exhausted iterator restarts it.
misconceptions.title: An exhausted iterator restarts

misconceptions.description: A generator body runs fully when the generator is created.
misconceptions.title: Generators run eagerly

misconceptions.description: Any syntactically nested loop is necessarily quadratic in input size.
misconceptions.title: Nested loops are always quadratic

misconceptions.description: Any single loop has linear complexity, irrespective of work in its body.
misconceptions.title: A single loop is always linear

misconceptions.description: A default object is created on the first call omitting that argument rather than when def executes.
misconceptions.title: Mutable default created on first call

misconceptions.description: append returns a new list and leaves its receiver unchanged.
misconceptions.title: append creates a new list

misconceptions.description: Python rejects mutable function defaults with TypeError.
misconceptions.title: Mutable defaults are forbidden

misconceptions.description: A closure's free-variable values freeze when its enclosing function returns.
misconceptions.title: Closure values freeze on return

misconceptions.description: Enclosing local bindings disappear on return, so closures cannot read them.
misconceptions.title: Closures lose enclosing bindings

misconceptions.description: A closure copies a loop variable's current value when the function is defined.
misconceptions.title: Closure captures the loop value

misconceptions.description: next(iterator, default) suppresses all exceptions, not just StopIteration.
misconceptions.title: next default suppresses all errors

misconceptions.description: The caller's except handler executes before the generator's finally during stack unwinding.
misconceptions.title: Caller handler runs before finally

misconceptions.description: Catching an escaped exception in the caller lets a generator resume after the unhandled raise.
misconceptions.title: Caught error resumes the generator

misconceptions.description: A list slice always copies the entire source list regardless of stop bound.
misconceptions.title: A slice copies the entire list

misconceptions.description: Sequential linear operations within a loop multiply to a quadratic per-iteration cost.
misconceptions.title: Sequential costs multiply

misconceptions.description: Ordinary list slices and membership use balanced search trees and take logarithmic time.
misconceptions.title: List slicing and membership are logarithmic

misconceptions.description: A name retains its first assigned value and later assignments are ignored.
misconceptions.title: First binding is permanent

misconceptions.description: An ordinary assignment adds the right-hand-side result to the target's previous value, as if using +=.
misconceptions.title: Assignment implicitly accumulates

misconceptions.description: A loop's if body executes for every visited item regardless of its condition.
misconceptions.title: Conditional body always executes

misconceptions.description: For an integer n, n % 2 == 0 identifies odd rather than even values.
misconceptions.title: Modulo parity is reversed

misconceptions.description: The update total = total + n discards the previous total and behaves like total = n.
misconceptions.title: Accumulator keeps only the last value

misconceptions.description: Matching one updated variable is sufficient for program equivalence even when another observable name aliases its original object.
misconceptions.title: Equivalence ignores aliases

misconceptions.description: Built-in list + mutates the old list, whereas built-in list += creates an independent list.
misconceptions.title: List addition mutation is reversed

misconceptions.description: List += mutates the list and then binds its target to None, confusing augmented assignment with the result of methods such as append.
misconceptions.title: List augmented assignment produces None

misconceptions.description: Any negative index raises IndexError instead of counting backward from the end of a built-in list.
misconceptions.title: All negative list indices are invalid

misconceptions.description: The right operand of and is evaluated even when its left operand is false.
misconceptions.title: Boolean and always evaluates both sides

misconceptions.description: index < len(items) alone guarantees safe list indexing even for arbitrary negative integer indices.
misconceptions.title: Upper-bound guard ensures valid negative indices

misconceptions.description: The stop bound of a two-bound slice is the number of elements to take, independently of its start bound.
misconceptions.title: Slice stop is a length

misconceptions.description: Evaluating a slice changes the source sequence to contain only the selected elements.
misconceptions.title: Slicing replaces its source

misconceptions.description: An index equal to the sequence length is valid, as though the upper indexing bound were inclusive.
misconceptions.title: Index equal to length is valid

misconceptions.description: Every string is true in a condition, including the empty string.
misconceptions.title: Every string is truthy

misconceptions.description: The text False inside a nonempty string makes that string false in a condition.
misconceptions.title: String spelling determines truth

misconceptions.description: An if/else statement executes both bodies rather than selecting one according to its condition.
misconceptions.title: Both if and else bodies execute

misconceptions.description: A function can never read a module-global name without a global declaration.
misconceptions.title: Reading globals requires a declaration

misconceptions.description: A local read before its first local assignment falls back to a same-named global.
misconceptions.title: Unbound locals fall back to globals

misconceptions.description: Reading a local before assignment is rejected when defining the function with SyntaxError rather than failing when the read executes.
misconceptions.title: Unbound locals are syntax errors

misconceptions.description: dict.get uses its default for a stored falsy value, not just a missing key.
misconceptions.title: Dictionary defaults replace falsy values

misconceptions.description: or replaces only None or the empty string with its right operand and passes all other values through unchanged, including numeric zero and empty containers.
misconceptions.title: or replaces only None and empty strings

misconceptions.description: or returns a bool describing combined truth rather than one of its operand values.
misconceptions.title: or returns a Boolean result

misconceptions.description: or always returns its right-hand operand even when the left operand is truthy.
misconceptions.title: or always takes its fallback
